Unlike standard 12-hour clocks, this dial shows the full 24-hour solar cycle. Solar Noon (zenith) is at the top (12:00), and Solar Midnight (nadir) is at the bottom (00:00). The sun moves clockwise along the path.

The dial displays five distinct astronomical phases:

• Daylight: Sun is above horizon (> 0°)
• Civil Twilight: 0° to -6° (natural light remains)
• Nautical Twilight: -6° to -12° (navigation stars visible)
• Astro Twilight: -12° to -18° (deep twilight)
• Night: Below -18° (full astronomical night with stars)

The sun marker orbits the 24-hour track. It is a solid white disc during daytime, and turns into a hollow ring at night when the sun is below the horizon. The radial beam points to current solar time.

The dots around the timeline ring mark 10 solar milestones:

• Morning: Astro Dawn, Nautical Dawn, Civil Dawn, Sunrise, and Solar Noon
• Evening: Sunset, Civil Dusk, Nautical Dusk, Astro Dusk, and Solar Midnight
All astronomical calculations use high-precision NOAA algorithms. Accurate twilight and solar times are computed specifically for your geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude).
